greeting: Ataniup atianut, Ataataup, Irniup, ammalu Anirniup Salumajuup. Ullaakkut, quviasungnarluni ilissinnik ilagiiktut, Ataniup uqausianik tusaaqatigilluta.
penitential:
Atanirjuat, ungahiktumit takujutit uummammi iluani. 
Kristu, qaujimajutit uummammi iluani. 
Atanirjuat, kinguvutit inuusiup aqqutingani.
psalm_response: Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
homily:
Imagine, for a moment, a quiet kitchen counter. It is a place of simple, everyday things: a bowl, a spoon, the hum of a refrigerator, the smell of something warm cooking. This is where Martha stood. She was busy, her hands moving from one task to another, her mind racing with the weight of all that needed to be done. It is a scene we know so well—the burden of the 'many things' that seem to demand our attention, the pressure to make everything just right, the feeling that if we stop for even a second, the whole world might unravel. 

Then, there is Mary. She sits at the feet of Jesus. She is still. She is listening. She is not worried about the meal or the serving or the expectations of the room. She has chosen the one thing that truly matters: the presence of the Lord. 

We often think of this Gospel as a choice between work and prayer, between being busy and being still. But look closer at the heart of the matter. Jesus does not tell Martha that her work is bad. He tells her she is 'anxious and worried about many things.' He is speaking to the ache behind the busyness. He is speaking to that part of us that believes our worth, or our safety, or our control over life depends entirely on how much we can manage, how much we can fix, how much we can hold together. 

Have you ever felt that weight? The morning comes, and before your feet even touch the floor, the list of 'must-dos' is already written in your heart. You want to be strong for your family. You want to be the one who keeps the house running, the one who holds the memories safe, the one who makes sure no one else has to carry the burden alone. You are like Martha, serving with love, but your heart is heavy with the worry of it all. You wonder if you are doing enough. You wonder if the love you pour out is being seen. 

Listen to the Lord’s voice in the middle of your kitchen, in the middle of your grief, in the middle of your long, quiet days. 'Martha, Martha.' He says your name twice. He is not scolding. He is calling you back to yourself. He is inviting you to set down the heavy load of 'many things' and simply be with Him. 

Think of Benjamin. Think of his brilliant, curious mind. He loved to dive into the complexities of the world—the logic of code, the architecture of a cloud environment, the intricate beauty of an airplane soaring high above the clouds. He was a boy who understood that the world is a place of systems and structures, a place where things work when they are built with care and precision. But more than that, Benjamin knew how to sit still in the heart of love. He knew how to share a giggle with his dad, how to look at the world with a smile that carried no fear, how to offer his own small treasures to help someone else. He didn't need to be 'busy' to be loved. He simply was. 

There is a profound truth in the way Saint Paul describes his own life in the first reading today. He speaks of a time when he was a 'zealot,' driven by his own intensity, his own desire to be right, his own way of doing things. But then, God intervened. 'When he, who from my mother’s womb had set me apart and called me through his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son to me.' Paul had to stop his own frantic journey to Damascus to finally see the Light. He had to learn that his life was not about what he could achieve, but about what God had already done. 

Maybe you are feeling like you need to justify your existence, or your pain, or your way of being in this world. Maybe you are still searching for the 'test' you think you need to pass, or the 'answer' that will finally make everything make sense. But listen to the Psalm: 'Truly you have formed my inmost being; you knit me in my mother’s womb.' You were known before you were born. You were known before you ever did a single thing to earn love. God does not need you to be perfect. He does not need you to be productive. He needs you to be His. 

There is a temptation, especially when we have walked through the valley of the shadow, to believe that we must carry the weight of the world on our own shoulders. We think that if we stop, if we sit at the feet of Jesus and just weep, or just breathe, or just be, that we are failing. We think we have to keep coding, keep building, keep planning, keep 'doing.' But the 'better part' is not a task. It is a relationship. It is the simple, quiet, unhurried act of letting God love you. 

To the parents who are carrying a love so deep it feels like it might break them: your love for Benjamin is a mirror of God’s love for him. Every time you remember his smile, every time you think of him dreaming of 'con chim airlines,' every time you feel the ache of his absence, you are not just remembering a boy who is gone. You are touching the reality of a soul who is more alive than ever, resting in the very Presence that Mary chose. 

And to his brother, who walks this path beside his parents: you are not alone. You have a brother who is cheering for you from the best seat in the house. You don't have to carry his legacy by being perfect or by doing everything right. You carry him by living. You carry him by being yourself, by exploring the world with the same curiosity he had, by letting your own heart be light, even when the days are long. 

There is a grace in stopping. There is a grace in admitting that we cannot fix everything, that we cannot control the future, that we cannot bring back what we have lost. But we can sit. We can sit at the feet of the One who knows our thoughts from afar. We can sit with the One who knitted us in our mother’s womb. We can sit and hear Him say our names, just as He said, 'Martha, Martha.' 

Do not be afraid of the silence. Do not be afraid of the empty chair. In that silence, the Lord is waiting. He is not asking you for more work. He is asking for your presence. He is asking you to let Him hold the things you are worried about, so that you can finally rest. 

Carry this with you today: you are enough. You are known. You are held. When the 'many things' start to crowd your mind, when the anxiety of the day begins to rise, just close your eyes for a moment. Picture the sky that Benjamin loved so much—that clear, open blue where the planes soar high and free. Let that be your prayer. Let your heart be the place where you sit at the feet of Jesus, and let Him be the one who does the serving, the one who does the healing, the one who does the loving. That is the better part. And it will never, ever be taken from you.
spiritual_communion: I believe that You, O Jesus, are in the most holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot now receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His peace, now and forever. Amen.
standing_petitions: Benjamin Vo-mut ammalu tamainnut inuujunnaqtunut, Ataniup qaumanningani inuuvigijaujut qasuqtuqtitauqullugit.
Tamainnut uqumaittumik atuqtunut, Atanirjuat quviasungnarnikkut ammalu niriunnikkut ikajuqullugit.

readings.label: Atuagait
readings.text: Nalunaittut: Tusaalauqsimajusi inuusirijauqsimajumik Judaism-mi, qanuq qivgaqtuqtuqsimajunga Ataniup ilagiinginnik ammalu sujulirijauqsimajunga. Pijunnautinik pijunnautiqalauqtunga Judaism-mi ammalu inuusiqaqtunga. Kisiani Atanirjuat, nunaqjuami inuusirijavut, qaujimajunga. Ataniup, naammagijaujuq, saqquqtittilauqtuq Irnini uvamnut, nalliutijumut. Isumagijaujungittunga inuinnanut, Jerusalem-mutlu aullalauqtunga. Arabia-mut aullalauqtunga, Damascus-mutlu utirama. Pingasuni ukiuni, Jerusalem-mut aullalauqtunga Cephas-mut, 15-nik ulluni. James-tuinnaq takulauqtara. Uqausiit, uqausiit, Ataniup takujanga. Syria-mut ammalu Cilicia-mut aullalauqtunga. Judea-mi ilagiit ilisimanngilaanga. Tusaajut: 'Taanna qivgaqtuqtuqsimajuaq, maanna uqausiqtuqtuq upperunnarnirmik.' Taanna Atanirjuat quviasuktaujuq.

readings.label: Psalm
readings.text: R. Atanirjuat, aqqutigiit aqqutikkuurutit. Atanirjuat, qaujimajutit uvamnik. Inuusirijavut qaujimajutit. R. Atanirjuat, aqqutigiit aqqutikkuurutit. Nunaqjuami inuusirijavut, inuusirijavut, inuusirijavut. R. Atanirjuat, aqqutigiit aqqutikkuurutit. Uummammi inuusirijavut, qaujimajutit. R. Atanirjuat, aqqutigiit aqqutikkuurutit.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus nunaqjuami, Martha-p tikisai. Mary, Jesus-up ataanut, tusaajuni. Martha, uqumaittumik, uqaqtuq: 'Atanirjuat, Mary ikajuinngilaanga.' Jesus uqaqtuq: 'Martha, Martha, uqumaittutit. Mary-p, taanna pijariaqaqtuq, qinirpaa.'

day: Tuesday of the Twenty-seventh Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.
